speaker: Doctor
text: Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing shortness of breath and increased abdominal girth? Have you noticed any recent weight changes or difficulty eating due to early satiety?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any pelvic pain, changes in your menstrual cycle, or pressure on your bladder causing frequent urination? Also, have you noticed any unexplained weight loss or loss of appetite despite the increase in abdominal size?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Doctor
text: Doctor: Given your shortness of breath and large ovarian mass, has your breathing difficulty been present while lying flat, suggesting fluid buildup? Also, do you have any history of similar issues in your family, particularly regarding ovarian or breast cancer?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol regularly. Works as a high school teacher.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any pain when urinating, or have you noticed changes in your bowel movements like constipation? REQUEST TEST: Pelvic Ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: CA-125 blood test.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic Ultrasound: Large mass in the right ovary, significant ascites present. CA-125 blood test: Level is Normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the large ovarian mass and ascites with a normal CA-125, are you experiencing any symptoms of megaloblastic anemia, such as extreme fatigue, a sore tongue, or numbness and tingling in your hands and feet? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count with Peripheral Smear. REQUEST TEST: Serum Folate and Vitamin B12 levels.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 8,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.8 g/dL, Platelets 275,000 /μL. Serum Folate and Vitamin B12 levels: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text: Doctor: Given the large ovarian mass and ascites with normal CA-125 and blood work, are you experiencing any skin changes like thickening of the palms or hair loss that might suggest a paraneoplastic syndrome? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal CT scan.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, night sweats, chest pain, or swelling in the legs. She has not noticed any changes in bowel or urinary habits.

speaker: Doctor
text: Doctor: With the normal CA-125 and blood work, I need to review the abdominal CT images to better characterize the ovarian mass and the extent of the ascites. Do you have any history of tuberculosis or other chronic infections, and have you noticed any skin changes on your face or upper body? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal CT scan.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Meigs Syndrome (benign ovarian fibroma with ascites and pleural effusion)
